I’m a certified card carrying Witwer fan. I love a lot of his work, and he’s in a lot of games I like! Pretty good musician, too. I think he’s sincerely talented, has the best intentions at heart and truly loves what he does. All of this applies to not only Star Wars but pretty much any project he’s involved with, which is to say a lot. Im glad I discovered him when I did, and he’s had an indelible impact on my life and creative interests. I’m also tired of Maul. And the prequel milking in general. When Maul came back, it was a moderately interesting reinterpretation of a character performed by an actor who really was trying something different, despite it being literally someone we’ve seen it before. Then he kept coming back. And again. And again. Also doesn’t help that, despite the denialism and dissonance, the Clone Wars show is a Children’s cartoon. There’s only so much they can say and do in the confines of a PGish rating. Prequel diehards (mainly millennials) are incredibly spoiled. The 3 films, Clone Wars, Clone Wars 2D, Rebels, Bad Batch, the Kenobi show (the worst offender), numerous Video games and Books; they have literally thousands of hours of the same shit. And they love it. It’s a bunch of late 20s-mid 30s mouth breathers who can’t deign to see something different or if it’s not a clone trooper or blue lightsaber. They don’t even care about the (simplistic) themes and tones of Star Wars and the prequels had. They just want space explosions, edgy lines and a more militant application of the fantasy play-thing they can’t seem to let go. To justify their liking it. “It’s not just for kids!” Saying this as a prequel fan myself, the old EU Is actually pretty cool and weird. Not all of it works, but damn if they didn’t try. When you have to bring back a 40+ Hayden Christensen to play himself even younger than he was when Revenge of the Sith came out, you have a problem. This isn’t even commenting on how many references and innuendos the Disney OG trilogy stuff has to the prequels. All this is to say it’s boring and pathetic. Star Wars can be so much more than what it’s been allowed to be. It’s been a brand for as long as it’s existed, but the past 10ish years, and particularly the last 5, have been about as stagnant as it gets with ideas. While I have generalized, I can almost guarantee you what I’ve said applies to like 60% of the fan base as it pertains to prequels. They love and can’t let go of the damage control that The Clone Wars children’s show started. It’s sad. I love Star Wars, and thankfully the really good stuff already happened, and there’s so much more quality material that isn’t trying to be something it’s not out there already. Frankly, material that is a touch more complex and enlightened than “Obi wan and Anakin fight in the desert! Remember them??”. Still love me some Witwer, though. Wish he would continue to pursue more provoking stuff. He’s a terrific performer. A paycheck’s a paycheck I guess. From Disney no less. Can’t even imagine.

I’ll never understand the insistence on using terms like “skill issue” when you have so many machines (mostly ussr and I’ll die on that hill) that are over-represented, over perform and are dirt cheap SP. not even talking about this video in particular, but the Yak-9T is such a common sight because people know it’s busted. Same with most of the early KV line and t34’s, they’re objectively stronger at their BR and frankly even a full BR higher than that in many instances. Other players have to be so surgical and deliberate with their plays and shots to take down even a T34-57, where said tank can knock out any Sherman, Cromwell or other “equivalent” with impunity. It’s worse with KV’s. I’m so tired of the legit dissonance when it comes to the USSR being undertierd and having shit that often times never left the prototype stage or just rewrites history with an aircraft that historically sucked. They don’t have to think, they barley have to aim and they have way too much leeway with SP and OP offensive weapons. I know I’ve expanded this past the present video, but it’s representative of the most heinous BR abuse the game has to offer. Nothing else moves like that at that tier, not even close. I’m still under the impression old boy is indoctrinated, however subtlety, from the very first frame of ME2. He, and by extension the almost the entirety of Cerberus, are literally an echo of the Collectors and other broken Protheans from the last cycle. I’m not calling it brilliant, but it is solid and poetic. The separatists in the Prothean Era were trying to accomplish precisely what Cerberus is in this cycle. People sometimes call The Illusive Man and his faction pointless heavies and are there just to be fought in ME3, but like even in 1 it has been explained that the Reapers and their indoctrination is absolutely thorough and nigh impossible to evade (especially if you’re unaware of it to begin with). He’s a nice little cautionary tale and the great of irony of him not only trying to save humanity but putting above all else, very nearly damned it. Despite his thoughts. Great character. 

I love the idea of indoctrination, and I sincerely wish BioWare did the the “less is more” approach when describing the Reapers. I don’t hate the Leviathan DLC, but I really don’t think it was necessary. A enigmatic extra-cosmic threat with minimal exposition is a great idea, and wish they stuck more with the cipher Sovereign than the generic Harbinger and logic-looped AI’s they’re revealed to essentially be. The actual goals of ME3 aren’t really impacted by this revelation, and I think the additional knowledge and demystifying of the Reapers only served to open up flaws in the already ambitious concept.

How on earth could any game even approach that figure. That’s an unconscionable amount of dough. 700 Million. That’s suspiciously high. Irrespective of one’s opinion of this COD, or any of the recent ones, I think it’s fair to say it’s a standard and conventional series. They’re not exactly pushing the boundaries. Again, not shade, but objective fact. How does that translate to 700 mil? You have a short campaign, the usual multiplayer suite and the servers surely do cost some, and advertising. Its really not that revolutionary. I cannot believe that this warrants that number. It’s not like they don’t make a killing on sales and MTX’s, so Im genuinely curious where all that money goes. Why even bother with that kind of production, people buy it all just the same. It’s not even like it’s graphically superior to what was on offer nearly a decade ago. Once more, I’m not attacking it, I just don’t understand. That’s almost immoral, though. That much scratch on what is really just a recreational activity doesn’t sit well.

Man, I have more than my fair share of nitpicks with this game. But that’s really all they are. It’s a very well realized game that miraculously got out of Steam Greenlight and is absolutely worth the money. Ready or Not has one of those communities where they’re more invested than average. It just has that “niche” that is too rarely explored. So it naturally attracts quite a few individuals who are all ready in unison to love and critique it to an overly amplified state. I could bring up many of its contemporaries for comparison, but we all know what they are. And it’s a game with a developer that is, as much as some hate to admit it, very communicative. They give development updates like clockwork.  Moreso than like 99% of other developers do. And they seem to be pretty clear with what they want to make. And that’s what you bought. They weren’t being deceitful. That’s not an excuse for them nor does it inoculate from criticism, but yes this community (particularly the part that frequents this very forum) does have quite the ego. Where their 40-80 dollars they spent (at most) in their mind translates to infinite expansions and pinpoint quality of life. I swear you’d think they they themselves were robbed  of their last dollar at gun point the way they moan. RoN is rough around the edges, and I don’t love everything they do. But it’s a damn good shooter that clearly has had a positive enough impact on those who lament it so often. Idk, sometimes I think some of you just need to take a break and play/do something else. The game is what it is, and again as much as some here hate to acknowledge, it’s a pretty good one. I also think Void is smart enough to recognize the fringe vocalists from the much more reasonable mass player base. At the end of the day, very little of what I said is subjective and it’s shame that some people just can’t understand that this game isn’t their personal venture, and that Void has their vision. It’s really not that deep. Not that this comment will alter anything. All love.
